- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment runs (sentiment < -0.30) — raise forecast baseline slightly.
- Overshoot after recent spikes — cap forecast peaks at 1.2x prior high or 1.1x recent high.
- Mean-revert forecasts if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative (sentiment -0.10 to 0.10) — adjust downward 0.5–1.0% per day.
- Lagged overreaction: if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is weak or mixed — cap upward revisions at 0.8x recent high unless sentiment > 0.30.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, reduce forecast mean by 0.5–1.5% per day to reflect bearish bias.
- Use sentiment as a volatility filter — if sentiment > 0.20, allow 10–15% forecast variance; if < -0.20, constrain to 5–10%.
